story_1.headline: RBI pulls the brake on its dollar drive
paragraphs: India's forex reserves touched a record near $729 billion in the week to August 21, up nearly $80 billion in about seven weeks, as the RBI leaned on FCNR(B) deposits and special swap facilities to pull dollars in rather than sell them outright. Roughly $73 billion has been mobilised this way, most of it landing straight on the central bank's balance sheet rather than the open market.

The rupee closed August near ₹95.4 to the dollar - still down sharply over two years despite the buffer-building. Brokerage Systematix argues the reserve build only delays the pressure, and pencils in a fresh depreciation path of about 6.5% a year as oil imports and a wide trade deficit keep dollar demand structurally high.

story_2.headline: The AI Boom meets the Stock Market
paragraphs: Wall Street closed out August with the Nasdaq up nearly 4% and the S&P 500 up over 2.6%, a rally still led overwhelmingly by AI infrastructure and chip names. That concentration turned into a liability this week: rising Treasury yields and a fresh spike in oil prices on US-Iran tensions hit chip stocks hardest as September trading opened.
A reminder of how much of the market's gains now sit on a small cluster of AI-linked bets - and how quickly that looks fragile when yields move.
